method: Every .ts file under the 12 listed src/ directories was read in full with the read tool (56 files). Line numbers below come from those reads; no README/doc file is used as evidence. Composition-entry lines (yaml) and production import lines outside the 12 packages were read separately and are cited only for the 'has a production caller' question.

mechanisms.name: fs-service-seam-and-target-identity
mechanisms.what: `FileSystem` (abstract `Service`, registered as `ctx.fs` by `super(ctx, 'fs')`) is the provider-neutral seam: `resolve()` maps a model path to a stable `FsTarget { targetKey, displayPath }`, and every other operation takes that target instead of a path. `processPath`, `processPathFromHostPath` (base returns `undefined`), `fileUrl`, and `contains` are the identity/containment primitives; `stat`/`lstat` return metadata only, `readText`/`streamText`/`readBytes`/`readByteRange`/`listDir` read, and only `writeText`/`editText` mutate. `sandboxMode` is a capability fact the tool layer reads (base returns `undefined`), and per-call `SandboxExecutionPolicy` is an optional last argument on the two mutations.
invariants: index.ts:14-15 'Consumers MUST NOT parse it or assume it is a local absolute path' (FsTargetKey doc, types.ts:13-15).
index.ts:81-84 'Targets must preserve identity across aliases; ... mutations are atomic.'

index.ts:94-99 sandboxMode is 'the capability fact the tool layer reads to advertise the escalation fields honestly', and widening is 'checked per call rather than encoded in this default-relative fact'.
constants: FsErrorCode union has 13 literal codes: FS_NOT_FOUND, FS_NOT_DIRECTORY, FS_NOT_TEXT, FS_NOT_REGULAR_FILE, FS_TOO_LARGE, FS_PERMISSION_DENIED, FS_SANDBOX_DENIED, FS_IO_ERROR, FS_STALE_VERSION, FS_NOT_OBSERVED, FS_AMBIGUOUS_EDIT, FS_EDIT_NOT_FOUND, FS_ABORTED (types.ts:175-188)
version token format is backend-owned; local backend emits `${dev}:${ino}:${size}:${mtimeNs}:${ctimeNs}` (fs-local/src/fsio.ts:74-76)

mechanisms.name: fs-error-taxonomy-and-harness-error-codes
mechanisms.what: `FsError extends HarnessError` carries a stable `FsErrorCode` plus `cause`; `dsh-fs` owns the vocabulary so the local backend, the sandbox backend, and the policy plugin raise the same codes instead of inventing message strings. `FsWriteIntent` is a two-arm union (`createIfAbsent` rejects an existing target with FS_NOT_OBSERVED; `replaceIfVersion` rejects absence or mismatch with FS_STALE_VERSION) and omission of the intent means unconditional create-or-overwrite, explicitly 'not a third union arm'. `FsObservation` is `{kind:'present',version}` or `{kind:'absent'}`, and the FsWriteOutcome/FsEditOutcome pair carries LF-normalized before/after text for a consumer-computed diff.
invariants: types.ts:118-122 'Omitting the intent from writeText means unconditional create-or-overwrite, not a third union arm.'
types.ts:139-140 before/after are 'LF-normalized storage text (the diff basis), never a diff'.
types.ts:49-51 'an absent observation authorizes only a guarded create, never an edit'.

mechanisms.name: fs-intent-waterfall-and-observed-events
mechanisms.what: `fs/write-intent` and `fs/edit-intent` are single-slot decision waterfalls: the first listener that returns a value owns the decision and does not call `next()`, while calling `next()` yields the bare provider's unconditional behaviour. `fs/observed` is a fire-and-forget emit whose listeners must be synchronous recorders - throws fail the tool call and returned promises are not awaited. `dsh-tool-fs` dispatches both waterfalls and emits `fs/observed` after a successful read or mutation; the base default passed as `next` is `() => undefined` for write and edit.
invariants: index.ts:50-56 'the first listener that returns an intent owns the decision rather than composing with peers'.
index.ts:67-70 'Listeners must be synchronous recorders: throws fail the tool call and returned promises are not awaited.'

mechanisms.name: fs-event-data-invariants
mechanisms.what: A Cordis companion plugin (`name = 'fs-invariant'`, `inject = ['invariants']`) installs a global `internal/dispatch` check over the three `fs/*` events. On every dispatch it re-validates that the event's first argument has a non-empty `targetKey` and `displayPath`; for `fs/observed` it additionally requires a non-empty `version` for `kind: 'present'` and rejects any kind outside `present`/`absent`. Registration goes through `ctx.invariants.register('@deepseek-ai/dsh-fs', install)`.
invariants: invariant.ts:16-17 'filesystem event targetKey must be non-empty' / 'filesystem event displayPath must be non-empty'.
invariant.ts:31 'fs/observed present version must be non-empty'.
invariant.ts:36 'fs/observed kind must be present or absent'.

mechanisms.name: local-target-realpath-identity
mechanisms.what: `resolveLocalTarget(cwd, path)` resolves a relative path against `cwd`, then prefers `fs.realpath(displayPath)` as the opaque `targetKey` so aliases/symlinks share one identity and one stale guard. When the file is absent it realpaths the nearest existing ancestor and re-appends the missing suffix (basename plus not-yet-created intermediate dirs) so the key stays stable across creation; on Windows it additionally stats the ancestor to restore the ENOTDIR semantic that Windows reports as ENOENT. `LocalFileSystem.resolve` maps the result to `{targetKey, displayPath}` and throws FS_ABORTED pre/post when the signal is already aborted; `processPath` returns the targetKey string, `contains` uses `path.relative` and rejects `..`/absolute results.
invariants: fsio.ts:139-141 'For a missing target, realpath the nearest existing ancestor and append the missing suffix, preserving identity across symlinked ancestors before and after creation.'
fs-local/src/index.ts:60-63 '`cwd` (a resolution default, NOT a containment boundary)'.
fsio.ts:147 'empty/whitespace-only throws FS_NOT_FOUND'.
constants: Windows-only ancestor stat repair gated on process.platform === 'win32' (fsio.ts:174)
root-termination fallback returns the raw displayPath as the key (fsio.ts:189)

mechanisms.name: local-version-token-from-stat-identity
mechanisms.what: `versionOf(info: BigIntStats)` builds the opaque `FsVersion` as `${dev}:${ino}:${size}:${mtimeNs}:${ctimeNs}` from a bigint stat, so any content, size, inode, or timestamp change moves the token. `probe` (stat, follows symlinks) and `probeNoFollow` (lstat) wrap the stat and return `null` for ENOENT and ENOTDIR only; `mode` is masked with `0o777`. A post-write probe miss falls back to the sentinel `missing:${targetKey}` rather than failing.
invariants: fsio.ts:216-218 'ENOENT (no such file) and ENOTDIR (a parent segment is a file) both mean the target is absent; any other metadata failure is a real permission/IO fault.'
fs-local/src/index.ts:266-267 the post-write probe miss 'requires a concurrent unlink between rename and stat' (v8-ignored fallback path).

mechanisms.name: local-text-read-binary-rejection
mechanisms.what: `readWholeText` stats for a regular file, reads the whole file with the abort signal translated to FS_ABORTED, rejects a NUL byte inside the first 8192 bytes as FS_NOT_TEXT, then decodes with `new TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal: true})` and maps the TypeError to FS_NOT_TEXT. `streamWholeText` gives the same text semantics chunk by chunk: it scans only the first 8192 bytes for NUL and feeds a single streaming fatal decoder so a multi-byte sequence split across chunks still decodes. Neither path normalizes line endings.
invariants: index.ts:186-188 'Read the whole regular text file as a single decoded string' (no normalization promised).
fsio.ts:2-4 'This provider layer returns validated UTF-8 text, streams large files, and rejects binary data'.
constants: BINARY_SAMPLE_BYTES = 8192 (fsio.ts:17), NUL scan window for both whole and streamed reads

mechanisms.name: local-bounded-byte-reads
mechanisms.what: `readWholeBytes(target, signal, maxBytes, internals)` first stats: a file larger than `maxBytes` fails with FS_TOO_LARGE before any content I/O, then it opens a read stream with `end: maxBytes` and re-checks the running byte count so a file that grows after the stat still cannot be buffered without bound. `readByteWindow(target, {offset, length})` opens the stream at `start: offset` with `end: offset + length - 1`, so only the window is buffered whatever the file size, and a window at/past EOF is empty. Both translate a mid-stream AbortError to FS_ABORTED and do no decoding or binary rejection.
invariants: fs/index.ts:203-206 'The bound lives at this seam so a backend can never buffer an unbounded file: a target known or discovered to exceed maxBytes fails with FS_TOO_LARGE instead of returning a truncated result.'
fs/index.ts:218-221 'The window is the bound here, not the file' and 'the caller's cap on length is the guard against unbounded buffering'.
constants: readWholeBytes stream `end: maxBytes` plus running `bytes > maxBytes` re-check (fsio.ts:407-418)

mechanisms.name: local-atomic-staged-write-and-fsync
mechanisms.what: `writeFileAtomic` (fsio.ts, exported from fs-local - a DIFFERENT implementation from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-atomic-write`) creates `<dir>/.<basename>.<pid>.<uuid>.tmpdir` with mode 0o700 (mkdir then chmod), opens `<basename>.tmp` inside it with `'wx'` and 0o600, writes the UTF-8 content, calls `handle.sync()` (fsync), optionally restores the destination's prior mode, then publishes by rename (POSIX) / `ReplaceFileW` (win32 with a prior mode) / `link()` (guarded create). The private staging directory is removed after the commit and a cleanup failure there is swallowed; any failure before the commit closes the handle and removes the staging dir, rethrowing the original FsError.
invariants: fsio.ts:556-560 'Atomically replace a file through a private, synced staging file in the same directory.'
fsio.ts:636-637 'The target is committed; owner-only staging residue cannot turn that write into a failure.'
fsio.ts:75-77 per-target lock serializes the read-guard-write window so 'concurrent writes/edits are deterministically ordered' (fs-local/src/index.ts:75-77).
constants: temp file mode 0o600 via open flag 'wx' (fsio.ts:603-604)
cleanup failure produces combined FS_NOT_FOUND message (fsio.ts:514, :647)

mechanisms.name: local-guarded-create-no-clobber-publication
mechanisms.what: For a `createIfAbsent` intent the publication step uses `link(tempPath, absolutePath)` - a hard link that cannot replace an existing file - instead of rename. On failure `throwGuardedCreateFailure` re-inspects the destination with `lstat`: an existing non-file yields FS_NOT_REGULAR_FILE, an existing file yields FS_NOT_OBSERVED, a naked EEXIST yields FS_NOT_OBSERVED, and anything else becomes FS_IO_ERROR with the original error as cause. This exists because 'Link errno values vary by platform and filesystem', so the errno alone cannot distinguish a collision from missing hard-link support.
invariants: fsio.ts:567-569 'publish with a hard-link no-replace primitive; a concurrent creator's file is preserved and this write is rejected with FS_NOT_OBSERVED'.
constants: FS_NOT_REGULAR_FILE when the inspected destination is not a file (fsio.ts:538)
FS_NOT_OBSERVED when the destination exists or the error is EEXIST (fsio.ts:540-551)
default inspectPublicationTarget is lstat(path, { bigint: true }) (fsio.ts:592-593)

mechanisms.name: windows-acl-preserving-file-replacement
mechanisms.what: `win32.ts` lazily loads `advapi32.dll`/`kernel32.dll` through koffi and binds `GetFileSecurityW`, `SetFileSecurityW`, `ReplaceFileW`, `GetLastError`. `readFileDaclWin32` reads the destination's self-relative DACL (two-call size probe then read), `copyFileDaclWin32` writes it onto the empty temp with DACL|PROTECTED_DACL so the staging parent's inheritance cannot widen it, and `replaceFileWin32` calls `ReplaceFileW` so the replaced file's ACL and replace metadata survive. In `writeFileAtomic` the DACL copy runs only when `platform === 'win32' && mode !== undefined`, publication uses `ReplaceFileW` on the same condition, and an ENOENT from ReplaceFileW falls back to plain `rename` because the temp already carries the protected DACL.
invariants: fsio.ts:558-560 'A new Windows file inherits the destination directory's DACL; a replacement copies the existing target's DACL onto the empty temp before writing and preserves the target descriptor at publication.'
win32.ts:104 'The destination must still be empty when confidentiality depends on this call.'
win32.ts:2-3 'Koffi loads lazily so non-Windows processes never open Win32 libraries.'
constants: errno mapping: 2/3 -> ENOENT, 5 -> EACCES, default -> EIO (win32.ts:60-70)
ReplaceFileW called with flags 0, backup/exclude/reserved null (win32.ts:124-131)

mechanisms.name: per-target-mutation-serialization-lock
mechanisms.what: `LocalFileSystem` keeps `locks: Map<string, Promise<unknown>>` keyed by `targetKey`; `withLock(targetKey, op)` chains `op` onto the previous tail promise (FIFO), stores a swallowed-result tail for the next waiter, and deletes the entry in `finally` only when it still owns the tail. Both `writeText` and `editText` run their whole probe -> guard -> read -> write -> probe sequence inside `withLock`, so the read-modify-write window cannot interleave.
invariants: fs-local/src/index.ts:75-77 'serializes mutating ops so the read-guard-write window cannot interleave, making concurrent writes/edits deterministically ordered (one wins, the rest see the new version and reject as stale)'.
fs-local/src/index.ts:243-245 'Still inside the per-target lock, so the read-match-write window is serialized and atomic.'
constants: lock scope is per-targetKey, in-process only (fs-local/src/index.ts:78)
the lock chain swallows a failed op for the next waiter (fs-local/src/index.ts:96)
writeText and editText both wrap in withLock (fs-local/src/index.ts:181, :236)

mechanisms.name: guarded-write-edit-stale-version-check
mechanisms.what: `writeText` probes the target, rejects a non-file with FS_NOT_REGULAR_FILE, then enforces the intent: `replaceIfVersion` requires the file to still exist and its version to equal the expected one (both mismatches -> FS_STALE_VERSION), and `createIfAbsent` with an existing file is refused as a blind overwrite with FS_NOT_OBSERVED. `editText` probes first and reports FS_STALE_VERSION for a missing target, FS_NOT_REGULAR_FILE for a non-file, and checks the version guard BEFORE literal matching so a stale edit cannot be misreported as FS_EDIT_NOT_FOUND or FS_AMBIGUOUS_EDIT.
invariants: fs-local/src/index.ts:238-241 'Stale guard before literal matching: an edit based on an old read reports FS_STALE_VERSION, not FS_EDIT_NOT_FOUND/FS_AMBIGUOUS_EDIT against newer content.'
fs-local/src/index.ts:194 'createIfAbsent onto an existing file: a blind overwrite - require a read first.'
fs-local/src/index.ts:197 'No expectation means an unconditional but still atomic write.'

mechanisms.name: crlf-normalized-literal-edit
mechanisms.what: `readForEdit` reads the file abortably, rejects any NUL byte as FS_NOT_TEXT, decodes fatally, returns LF-normalized content plus the detected line-ending style (sampled from the first 4096 characters; CRLF wins only when crlfCount > lfCount). `applyLiteralEdit` normalizes oldString/newString, rejects an empty oldString as FS_EDIT_NOT_FOUND, counts non-overlapping occurrences with indexOf, rejects zero matches as FS_EDIT_NOT_FOUND and >1 without `replaceAll` as FS_AMBIGUOUS_EDIT, and returns the text replaced via split/join. `editText` then restores the original style with `restoreLineEndings` (which re-normalizes first so CRLF is never doubled) before the atomic write, while the returned `before`/`after` stay LF-normalized as the diff basis.
invariants: fsio.ts:660-663 'Collapse CRLF to LF - the canonical in-memory form every edit/diff basis uses. Lone \r bytes (not followed by \n) are left untouched.'
fsio.ts:677-681 'LF returns the content unchanged; CRLF re-normalizes first so an already-CRLF sequence is never doubled to \r\r\n.'
fs-local/src/index.ts:222-224 'a CRLF overwrite must not read as every line changed'.

mechanisms.name: bounded-overwrite-diff-basis
mechanisms.what: `writeText` captures a contextual-diff basis only when the outgoing content is below `diffBasisMaxBytes` and the target already existed, via `readTextForDiff`, which enforces the bound on the OPENED descriptor rather than a prior path stat: it stats the handle, returns null for a non-file or `size >= maxBytes`, allocates `openedSize + 1` bytes to detect growth after the stat, reads in 64 KiB chunks, returns null when the byte count differs from the opened size, returns null on a NUL byte or invalid UTF-8, and otherwise returns LF-normalized text. I/O failure of the optional basis returns null while cancellation (FsError) still propagates.
invariants: fsio.ts:721-726 'The bound is enforced on the opened descriptor rather than a prior path stat, so concurrent external replacement or size changes cannot make this helper buffer more than maxBytes.'
fsio.ts:778-781 'a committed write must not fail for a presentation-only pre-read'.
fsio.ts:729 'aborts the read (FS_ABORTED); cancellation propagates, unlike I/O failure'.

mechanisms.name: local-directory-listing-stable-order
mechanisms.what: `listDirectory` probes the target (missing -> FS_NOT_FOUND, non-directory -> FS_NOT_DIRECTORY), reads entries with `readdir(..., { withFileTypes: true, encoding: 'utf8' })`, sorts them by `name.localeCompare`, and for each child resolves a child target and probes it, emitting `{name, type, target, version?, size?}` (size only for regular files). Non-ENOENT/ENOTDIR/EPERM failures are translated by `listingIoError` into FS_IO_ERROR with the original as cause. Abort is checked before, after listing, and between children.
invariants: fs/index.ts:230-232 'Returns resolved child targets plus cheap metadata only; never reads file contents.'
fsio.ts:277-280 'file contents are never read' and listing aborts with FS_ABORTED 'checked between children'.
constants: permission errors -> FS_PERMISSION_DENIED (fsio.ts:265); anything else -> FS_IO_ERROR (fsio.ts:266)

mechanisms.name: read-before-write-observation-policy
mechanisms.what: `fs-observation-policy` registers NO service and has no `inject`: `apply()` builds one `ObservedStateGate` per plugin instance holding `WeakMap<owner, Map<targetKey, FsObservation>>`, where the owner is derived from the opaque event actor as `actor.agent.session`. It occupies the `fs/write-intent` slot (unseen or confirmed-absent -> `createIfAbsent`, present -> `replaceIfVersion` at the observed version) and the `fs/edit-intent` slot (no owner or unseen -> FS_NOT_OBSERVED, absent -> FS_NOT_FOUND, present -> `{version}`), and it records `fs/observed` synchronously. Both waterfalls are deferred through `Promise.resolve().then` so a throw rejects rather than escaping synchronously. Disposal clears all state for HMR.
invariants: index.ts:2-5 'Without this plugin, tools retain the bare provider's unconditional mutation behavior.'
index.ts:116 and :121 'occupy the single decision slot - do NOT call next()'.
index.ts:124-126 'fs/observed must remain synchronous and non-throwing: emit does not await promises, and successful mutations have already committed.'
constants: owner = `actor.agent.session`, `undefined` for a direct call with no agent (index.ts:36-41)
unseen edit -> FS_NOT_OBSERVED 'edit requires reading "..." first' (index.ts:82)

mechanisms.name: fs-sandbox-per-call-write-confinement
mechanisms.what: `SandboxedFileSystem extends LocalFileSystem`, so all read/list/atomic-write mechanics are inherited verbatim and only `writeText`/`editText` are fenced. `checkedTarget` resolves the effective policy (per-call or `ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve()`), returns the caller's target unfenced for `danger-full-access`, throws FS_SANDBOX_DENIED for `read-only`, and for `workspace-write` RE-canonicalizes the target with `this.resolve(displayPath)` and requires it under some root of `writableRoots(policy)`, returning the FRESH target so the checked identity is the mutated one. The class advertises `sandboxMode` from `ctx.sandboxPolicy.defaultMode` and requires that service (`inject = ['sandboxPolicy']`).
invariants: index.ts:10-18 'The fence is a policy check in TRUSTED code over a MODEL-CONTROLLED path, NOT a kernel boundary ... containment, not a security boundary; kernel-grade isolation of untrusted CODE stays ctx.shell's job'; the residual symlink TOCTOU is 'narrowed by re-canonicalizing immediately before delegating and is accepted for this threat model'.
index.ts:111-114 'return the EXACT target the mutation must use, so the checked identity is the mutated one (no check-here-write-there TOCTOU)'.
index.ts:7-8 'Reads pass through untouched: every mode permits reading.'
constants: read-only denial message: 'file access denied under read-only mode' (index.ts:127)
workspace-write denial message: 'file access denied under workspace-write mode' (index.ts:141)

mechanisms.name: fs-containment-lexical-then-identity-check
mechanisms.what: `isPathUnder(path, root, caseSensitive = process.platform !== 'win32')` first tries a purely lexical comparison (optional lowercasing, root plus separator prefix), then falls back to filesystem identity: it stats the root, walks the target's ancestors with `statIfPresent` (ENOENT/ENOTDIR -> undefined), and returns true when any ancestor has the same `dev` and `ino` as the root; the walk terminates at the filesystem root. This recognizes Windows long-name/8.3 aliases and casing differences without weakening containment to a textual approximation.
invariants: containment.ts:2-5 'Canonical spellings take the fast lexical path; filesystem identity supplies the conservative fallback for alias-equivalent roots such as Windows 8.3 names and casing.'
containment.ts:50-51 the fallback exists to recognize aliases 'without weakening containment to a textual approximation'.
constants: identity comparison is dev+ino equality only (containment.ts:42-44)
ancestor walk terminates when dirname(ancestor) === ancestor (containment.ts:72-73)

mechanisms.name: tool-read-windowed-line-render
mechanisms.what: The `read` tool validates `file_path`/`offset`/`limit` (`limit` defaults to and may not exceed the configured `readLimit`), resolves the target once via `resolveRegularReadTarget` (which emits `fs/observed absent` and throws FS_NOT_FOUND on a miss, and rejects non-regular files), and uses that single stat for type, size routing, and the observed version. It streams when `size` is undefined or `>= readStreamMinSize`, otherwise reads whole, then `buildWindow` scans to an exact total line count while keeping only the requested window, truncating each line past `maxLineLength` with a suffix and stopping at `maxBytes` with `truncatedByBytes` set; the page is rendered into a `<path>/<type>/<content>` envelope with a continuation footer, and `fs/observed present` is emitted after success.
invariants: read.ts:139-140 'One stat: absence observation OR type check + size routing + present version. A concurrent write can only make a later guarded mutation fail stale and require reread.'
read-render.ts:2-4 'Chunk scanning caps the current line, so even one newline-free giant line cannot grow memory without bound.'
read-render.ts:117 'One char past the truncation point is enough to prove a line overflows.'
constants: READ_LIMIT = 2000 default and maximum lines per read (read.ts:15)
READ_MAX_LINE_LENGTH = 2000 chars per line before '... (line truncated to N chars)' (read-render.ts:11, :70)
READ_MAX_BYTES = 50 * 1024 output byte cap for the page (read-render.ts:14)
offset past EOF -> FS_NOT_FOUND unless truncatedByBytes or (0 lines and offset 1) (read-render.ts:96-97)
offset defaults to 1 and limit to maxLimit (read.ts:57-58)

mechanisms.name: tool-write-atomic-outcome-and-hunk-diff
mechanisms.what: The `write` tool validates a non-blank `file_path` (empty content is legitimate), resolves the per-call sandbox policy BEFORE anything executes, resolves the target with the policy workspace root as cwd, then obtains a single-slot `fs/write-intent` (bare default `undefined` = unconditional, no stat), calls `ctx.fs.writeText`, maps the error through `sandbox.mapError` + `remediateFsError`, emits `fs/observed present` with the produced version, and returns `{path, operation, before, after}`. The presentation meta carries one three-line-context hunk per applied change computed with the `diff` package's `structuredPatch`; a null `before` (create or declined basis) yields an empty diff list and the result presenter falls back to the call args.
invariants: write.ts:112-113 'Single-slot decision: the policy plugin produces createIfAbsent/replaceIfVersion; the bare default is undefined (unconditional). No stat.'
diff.ts:40-42 'The unified-diff marker for a missing trailing newline annotates the patch, not the content - skip it so it never leaks into a diff block.'
diff.ts:31 'one diff per applied hunk, in file order; empty when the texts are identical'.

mechanisms.name: tool-edit-literal-replace-with-version-guard
mechanisms.what: The `edit` tool rejects a blank `file_path`, an empty `old_string`, and `old_string === new_string` ('a guaranteed no-op edit'), resolves the sandbox policy first, resolves the target, and inside a try obtains the `fs/edit-intent` waterfall (which can itself throw FS_NOT_OBSERVED for an unread target) and calls `ctx.fs.editText` with `{oldString,newString,replaceAll}`. Both the intent refusal and the provider's guarded-mutation failure go through `sandbox.mapError` + `remediateFsError`, then `fs/observed present` is emitted with the edited version. The success text distinguishes single vs replace-all wording, and the presentation meta is the applied hunk diff.
invariants: edit.ts:119-124 'the bare default never manufactures a version basis. The intent slot itself can throw FS_NOT_OBSERVED for an unread target, so it sits inside the try'.
edit.ts:41-42 'old_string !== new_string (an equal pair would be a guaranteed no-op edit)'.
edit.ts:148-149 the call-time diff card is derived from the args because a call-time presenter has no prior content.
constants: single-match wording vs 'All occurrences were successfully replaced.' (edit.ts:64-68)

mechanisms.name: session-workspace-cwd-resolution
mechanisms.what: `sessionCwd(exec, requestedPath)` returns the calling agent's `exec.agent.session.header.cwd`, and only when either the cwd or the requested path contains a `..` path segment does it canonicalize the cwd with `canonicalPath` so a symlinked cwd's filesystem identity becomes observable. A non-agent call returns `undefined`, deliberately leaving the fallback to the provider rather than reading `process.cwd()` at the tool boundary. `sessionResolveOptions` returns `{cwd, signal}` for every model-facing fs tool, preferring a resolved per-call `policyWorkspaceRoot` over the session cwd.
invariants: session-cwd.ts:2-6 'each session's read/write/edit act on its workspace, not the server's launch directory. Non-agent calls return undefined, leaving the fallback in the provider rather than reading process.cwd() at the tool boundary.'
session-cwd.ts:18-19 'parent traversal makes a symlinked cwd's filesystem identity observable'.
constants: policyWorkspaceRoot takes precedence over the session cwd (session-cwd.ts:40)
signal is always forwarded from exec.signal (session-cwd.ts:43)

mechanisms.name: guarded-mutation-error-remediation
mechanisms.what: `remediateFsError(error, displayPath)` rewrites exactly two codes for the model: FS_NOT_OBSERVED becomes `cannot modify "<path>": file has not been read - read the file, then retry` (replacing policy/provider text) and FS_STALE_VERSION keeps the provider's reason and appends `- re-read the file, then retry`. Both preserve the original code for machine routing and keep the original error as `cause`; any other value passes through untouched. It runs after `FsSandboxController.mapError`, so a sandbox denial (already mapped to the shared `[sandbox: ...]` marker) is not rewritten.
invariants: error.ts:12-16 'FS_STALE_VERSION keeps the provider's reason and appends its re-read remedy. FS_NOT_OBSERVED replaces operation-specific policy/provider text with one path-aware reason and read remedy.'

fs/tool-fs/src/sandbox.ts:114-117 the structured FS_SANDBOX_DENIED code must survive 'because ToolRuntime populates result.error only for HarnessError instances, so a plain Error would strip the code'.
constants: FS_NOT_OBSERVED text: 'cannot modify "...": file has not been read - read the file, then retry' (error.ts:25)
FS_STALE_VERSION suffix: ' - re-read the file, then retry' (error.ts:31)

mechanisms.name: fs-sandbox-escalation-approval-controller

mechanisms.name: atomic-write-sibling-rename-with-windows-retry
mechanisms.what: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-atomic-write`'s `writeFileAtomic(filename, content, {mode, dirMode?})` creates parent directories, writes a random-suffix sibling ``${filename}.${randomBytes(6).toString('hex')}.tmp`` with `flag:'wx'` (which refuses to follow a symlink planted at the temp path) and the caller's mode, then renames it over the target so readers see either the old or the new complete content and the replaced file ends up with exactly the stated mode. On Windows, transient `EACCES`/`EBUSY`/`EPERM` renames are retried with exponential backoff (20 ms doubling to a 200 ms cap, at most 8 retries); on any remaining failure the temp is removed and the error rethrown. Crash durability (fsync) is explicitly out of scope. This is a different implementation from `fs-local`'s synced, DACL-aware `writeFileAtomic`.

mechanisms.name: cross-process-file-lock
mechanisms.what: `withFileLock(filename, operation, {waitMs?})` serializes cross-process writers of one file through a `wx`-created sibling ``<filename>.lock`` holding the pid; readers stay lock-free because the rename commit is atomic. Contention is `EEXIST` directly, or `EPERM` only when a fresh `lstat` confirms the lock path exists (Windows exclusive-create behaviour, without hiding an unrelated permission failure). Contention backs off exponentially from 20 ms to a 200 ms cap and fails with a timed-out error once the deadline (now + `waitMs ?? 2000`) passes. The lock is released in `finally`; a contender never removes an existing lock because file age cannot prove the owner stopped.

mechanisms.name: workspace-file-observation-change-feed-host
mechanisms.what: `WorkspaceChangeFeed` owns one `fs/observed` subscription per host context and fans each emission to every open `changes` generation; the OS is not watched, only instrumented filesystem operations report. `follow` registers the follower BEFORE awaiting `fs.resolve(workspaceRoot)` so nothing observed during resolution is lost, resolves under the generation's signal (a rejection caused by the abort ends quietly), yields one `{kind:'ready'}`, then yields `change` frames whose target passes `ctx.fs.contains(root, target)` and whose absolute path comes from `processPath`. Each generation has a `Deque` queue and a wake callback; the follower is removed and closed in `finally`, so anything still queued is dropped with the generation.
invariants: changes.ts:2-5 'every fs/observed emission whose target lies inside a generation's workspace root becomes one frame of that generation. Instrumented filesystem operations emit these observations; the operating system is not watched.'
changes.ts:42-43 'Registered before the root resolves, so nothing observed while it does is missed; the root only filters at drain time.'
types.ts:117-120 'Frames report observations, not deltas: a consumer already holding version learns nothing new from the frame and can ignore it.'
constants: one `ready` frame per generation before any change frame (changes.ts:55)
abort during resolve is swallowed only when signal.aborted (changes.ts:50-53)
queued observations are dropped when the generation closes (changes.ts:94)

mechanisms.name: client-file-resource-provider-and-change-fanout
mechanisms.what: The client half registers a `file` resource provider over `remote.workspaceFiles`: `createFileResourceProvider` parses the address with `parseFileAddress`, refuses an unparsable address with `workspace-file/unsupported-address` and an `absolute` address (no Session to authorize the Host call) with `workspace-file/unknown-workspace`, then waits for the change feed's `ready` before the first `stat`, binds the feed to the Host-reported `absolutePath`, and re-stats on any notice that could mean stale content. `ChangeFeed` keeps ONE Host `changes` stream per session, opens it when the first follower arrives (after the predecessor stream has settled, so a session never has two Host streams), fans frames to followers by normalized path key, and disposes the stream when the last follower leaves; teardown awaits every stream still closing.
invariants: provider.ts:17-21 'Failures travel as ok: false frames, never as thrown errors: the Remote face does not reject ... A failed stat does not end the stream: the next write stats again.'
change-feed.ts:119-121 'A predecessor still closing finishes first, so one session never has two Host streams open at once.'
client/index.ts:28-29 'Teardown waits for every session stream still closing, so the plugin leaves no Host stream behind.'
constants: two error codes raised by the Client and never by the Host: workspace-file/unsupported-address, workspace-file/unknown-workspace (client/types.ts:34, :40)
path key normalization replaces backslashes with '/' (change-feed.ts:22-24)
a change whose version equals the current one is skipped (provider.ts:86)

mechanisms.name: workspace-controller-remote-commands
mechanisms.what: `WorkspaceController` owns the `workspace` Remote namespace and delegates every verb to `WorkspaceCommands`, which serializes each mutation on its own `operationTail` so title-ownership checks cannot interleave: `create` resolves by canonical path first (idempotent, `created:false`), `rename` rejects a blank title (`gateway/bad-request`) and any title already used by another workspace (`workspace/name-conflict`), `delete` maps an unknown id to `workspace/not-found`, `insertBefore` maps `WorkspaceOrderInvalidError` to `workspace/not-found`, `insertSessionBefore` maps `WorkspaceMoveInvalidError` to `workspace/move-invalid`, and `archiveSession` maps `WorkspaceUnknownSessionError` to `session/not-found`. The controller also loads `DirectoryPickerController` as a child plugin, so a host without a picking backend registers no picking namespace.
invariants: commands.ts:61 'Rename one Workspace after serializing title ownership checks.'
index.ts:45-48 'The child stays pending until a picking backend is composed, so a host without one registers no picking namespace instead of answering an unservable verb.'
commands.ts:49 a pre-existing RemoteError is rethrown as itself rather than re-wrapped.
constants: error codes: workspace/invalid-path, workspace/name-conflict, workspace/move-invalid, workspace/not-found, session/not-found (commands.ts:51, :76, :133, :158, :178)

mechanisms.name: workspace-follow-baseline-stream
mechanisms.what: `WorkspaceFeed` snapshots the registry (`knownIds`, `order`, `archived`) at construction and listens to `domain/changed`. Each `follow` generation yields exactly one `baseline` frame from the live registry and then ordered increments: registry-global state puts produce `upsert` frames for newly known ids, an `order` frame when the order changed, and an `archived` frame when the archive set changed; a `workspaces`-table put produces an `upsert` only for an already-known id, and a delete produces `remove` only for a known id. A committed registry that references a missing workspace throws. Each follower queues frames in a `Deque` and waits on an abort-aware promise.
invariants: types.ts:125 'Workspace state stream; every generation starts with exactly one baseline.'
feed.ts:19-22 'Project one authoritative Workspace entity into its Remote value' - the view is detached (sessionIds copied).
feed.ts:121-126 table deletes/puts for unknown ids are ignored rather than resurrecting removed rows.
constants: baseline is read synchronously from the registry, not from the queue (feed.ts:70-75)
unknown-but-committed workspace throws 'committed Workspace registry references missing Workspace' (feed.ts:106)
only `change.table === ''` (global) puts are treated as order/archive carriers (feed.ts:97-99)

mechanisms.name: directory-picker-capability-gating
mechanisms.what: `DirectoryPickerController` backs the `directoryPicker` Remote namespace over the abstract `ctx.directoryPicker` seam and refuses any verb the composed backend cannot serve: `requireCapability(kind, method)` inspects `capability().kind` and throws `directory-picker/unavailable` naming the kind the backend does serve. `createDirectory` validates a zod request first (one non-blank path segment, not '.'/'..', no slash or backslash) -> `gateway/bad-request` with the issues, then maps the seam's closed `DirectoryPickerErrorCode` vocabulary onto `directory-picker/unreadable|exists|create-failed` with the offending path. `cancellableFailure` answers `gateway/cancelled` when the caller's signal aborted BEFORE the business classification runs.
invariants: directory-picker.ts:36-39 'this controller carries the wire verbs: one composed backend serves either the native chooser or the browse primitives, and a verb the composition cannot serve is refused rather than approximated.'
directory-picker.ts:153-154 'An abort is the caller's own timeout or disconnect, not a backend failure, so it answers gateway/cancelled before the business classification runs.'
constants: rejected directory names: blank/'.'/'..' or containing / or \ (directory-picker.ts:22-24)
unavailable message names the served kind (directory-picker.ts:114)

mechanisms.name: client-workspace-model-race-resolution
mechanisms.what: `ClientWorkspaceModel` owns the Client projection: it merges unary command echoes immediately (upsert/remove/installOrder), installs a stream baseline by replacing everything, and resolves unary-vs-stream races with generation counters - a locally optimistic reorder is only reconciled when both `orderRequestGeneration` and `orderFrameGeneration` are unchanged, and an upsert whose incoming `updatedAt` is older than the installed row is dropped. Removed ids go into a `removedIds` set because Host ids are never reused, so delayed data cannot resurrect a removed row. Invalidations coalesce through a microtask with a generation guard, and `WorkspaceController` (client) exposes the command facade while `createWorkspaceStateStream` wraps the Remote stream in a `RemoteSnapshotStream` that maps `baseline` to replace and increments to update.
invariants: model.ts:66 'Host Workspace ids are never reused, so delayed data cannot resurrect a removed row.'
model.ts:60-63 'Latest local reorder request; only its unary echo may install order' and 'Increments on stream orders so a later remote commit outranks an older unary echo.'
index.ts:82-84 a stream that ended after being accepted is treated as a retryable `RemoteStreamCarrierError`, not a terminal failure.
constants: upsert drops an older projection via `Date.parse(view.updatedAt) < Date.parse(installed.updatedAt)` (model.ts:282)
invalidation coalesced on queueMicrotask with a generation guard (model.ts:327-331)

packages/fs/fs.note: Abstract `FileSystem` Service at `ctx.fs` plus the error/type vocabulary and one invariant companion: it declares contracts and three events but implements no filesystem I/O (all 13 abstract members).

packages/fs/fs-local.note: Owns every local mechanic: realpath identity, binary-rejecting text reads, bounded byte reads, synced staged atomic writes with Windows ACL preservation, per-target mutation lock, stale guards, CRLF-normalized literal edits, bounded diff basis, stable listings.

packages/fs/fs-observation-policy.note: Not plumbing: it holds the WeakMap observed-state and decides both intent waterfalls; it registers no Service and has no `inject`, so it is pure policy over `fs/*` events.

packages/fs/fs-sandbox.note: Thin but substantive: `SandboxedFileSystem` overrides only the two mutations to fence them per call, and `containment.ts` implements the lexical-then-identity containment test used by that fence.

packages/fs/tool-fs.note: Owns schemas, validation, read windowing/rendering, the escalation+approval controller, error remediation, session-cwd resolution, image sniffing/attachment commit, and result presentation meta; it holds no filesystem implementation.

packages/fs/tool-fs-search.note: Owns ripgrep argv construction, complete-stdout parsing, per-line and per-item retention, oversize-page sampling, formatted spill, presentation meta, and the timeout/grace/stderr budget declarations; deliberately does NOT inject `fs`.

packages/fs/tool-present.note: Small but real logic: validates an open turn, cwd, and 1..maxFiles regular files, then appends a durable `deliverables/presented` session event only for a non-error result. Registers one tool and one `tools/result` listener.

packages/fs/tool-str-replace-editor.note: Registers one multi-command tool with its own absolute-path rule, unique-literal-match logic, line insertion, shallow listing, and output clipping, plus a duplicated MutationPolicy sandbox split.

packages/util/atomic-write.note: Independent of the fs domain: its `writeFileAtomic` is a separate implementation from fs-local's (no fsync, no DACL handling, Windows rename retries instead) and `withFileLock` provides the cross-process writer lock. Has production callers outside this domain.

packages/api/workspace-files.note: Two halves: the Host service implements read/page/window/stat/list plus the workspace-scoped observation feed with its own confinement and lstat gates; the Client half implements the `file` resource provider and the per-session change fan-out. Not plumbing.

packages/workspace/workspace.note: Substantive domain logic: canonical-path canon, durable registry order with a pending-mutation marker and rollback, header-validated session membership with durable pruning, and a domain/cache invariant companion.

packages/api/workspace-controller.note: Host side is a Remote facade over the registry with serialized commands, stable wire error mapping, the follow baseline stream, and the directory-picker capability gate (mostly delegation, but the mapping/ordering logic is real); the Client model carries the race-resolution logic and the snapshot-stream wiring.
